issues.issue: The King returns requires 3 but supplies no explicit instruction for a player with fewer than 3 eligible pieces across non-King regions and court.
issues.limit: The same page explicitly handles a shortfall for Decay of Authority, but does not state that this exception generalizes. Do not invent a return-as-many-as-possible rule as an express rule of The King returns.

issues.issue: The remove-2 paragraph relaxes the 2-piece condition when the player has at most 1 in any region, but does not expressly explain zero-piece cases or a player whose only region pieces are in the King’s region.
issues.limit: The protected-location prohibition is explicit. The source does not permit taking protected pieces and does not clearly specify a legal region choice or exact shortfall procedure in these edge cases.

issues.issue: The all-from-one-region paragraph exempts a player with no pieces in any region, but does not explicitly exempt or give a selection procedure for a player whose only region pieces are in the King’s region.
issues.limit: Returning pieces from the King’s region remains prohibited; do not invent an exception or an additional exemption.

issues.issue: For both secret removals, fellow players receive the removal obligation while all players receive the simultaneous-selection instruction. The source does not explicitly reconcile those scopes.
issues.limit: Opponents-only removal is directly supported by card and heading. Claiming the actor also removes pieces, or that the actor definitely does not select a disk, goes beyond an explicit resolved statement in this source.

would_resolve: Official publisher/designer errata or clarification for this classic English edition covering each issue; a later edition alone cannot silently replace authority.

essential_branches.title: The King returns: fewer than three eligible Caballeros
source_references: PDF p.9, The King returns detailed explanation and printed card
essential_branches.source_problem: The detailed explanation requires each player to return three own Caballeros from regions and/or court while forbidding King's region and Castillo. Unlike the adjacent three-from-court Decay card, it gives no shortfall procedure.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: A player's court plus all non-King board regions contain only zero, one, or two of that player's Caballeros; remaining pieces are in provinces, Castillo, or King's region.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: Whether that player returns all eligible pieces, returns none, prevents execution of the entire action, or follows another procedure changes piece counts and the action's effect on the other players.
essential_branches.summary_reason: States the exact requirement, ownership, turn order and excluded origins, and expressly says the shortfall rule is absent.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: For this edition's The King returns action, specify the complete procedure for a player with 0, 1, or 2 eligible own Caballeros, and whether a shortage affects execution against other players. Confirm protected pieces remain unavailable.

essential_branches.title: Return one from each player: a player has no eligible regional Caballero
source_references: PDF p.9, You send 1 Caballero ... from each player
essential_branches.source_problem: The selector must choose one from every player, including themselves, but only from regions and never King's region or Castillo. No exception covers an absent eligible piece.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: One player's pieces are all in court, provinces, King's region, and/or Castillo.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: The source does not state whether to omit that player, cancel the action, or apply another fallback. Court pieces are not an authorized substitute.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Correctly identifies the selecting player's choice, includes their own piece, and discloses the missing fallback.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: If any player has no Caballero in an eligible non-King region, is that player skipped while one is returned for every other eligible player, or is another procedure required?

essential_branches.title: Secretly return two: no legal selected region or unavailable two-piece region
essential_branches.source_problem: Selection must contain at least two own pieces; the one-piece fallback applies when the player has at most one in any region. No procedure covers zero eligible pieces. A further collision occurs when the only region containing two or more is protected, while eligible regions contain single pieces: the literal fallback condition is false, but no legal two-piece selection exists.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: An affected fellow player has no eligible regional pieces; alternatively, two own pieces are in King's region and one is in another region. If 'all players select' includes the selector, their lack of a legal qualifying region creates the same selection problem.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: No selection, choosing an empty region, selecting a protected region without removal, returning one eligible piece, and aborting the action are different procedures; returning the protected pieces violates an explicit rule.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Preserves the two/one distinction and acknowledges missing eligible-region procedures and the protected-only case. It does not expressly illustrate the mixed protected-two/eligible-one case, but supplies no invented fallback.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Define selection and return for zero eligible pieces, protected-only pieces, and a protected two-piece region plus only eligible single-piece regions. Does 'at most one in any region' mean any eligible non-King region? Specify whether empty/no-op disks are permitted and which players must submit them.

essential_branches.title: Secretly return all from one region: protected-only ownership
source_references: PDF p.10, secretly return all from one region
essential_branches.source_problem: A selected region must contain at least one own Caballero. A player with no Caballeros in any region is expressly unaffected, but the rule does not expressly extend that exception to a player whose only regional pieces occupy King's region.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: An affected player has Caballeros in King's region and none in other board regions.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: The literal nonparticipation exception does not apply, the only occupied selection cannot legally lose pieces, and empty selections fail the occupancy requirement.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Accurately states the exception and occupancy rule and explicitly identifies protected-only selection as unresolved.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Is a player with no Caballeros outside King's region treated as unaffected for this action? If so, must they still set/reveal a disk, and what selections are legal for that no-op participation?

essential_branches.title: The Court: fewer than two Caballeros in provinces
essential_branches.source_problem: The Court only says to move two own Caballeros from provinces to court. The power-card recruitment fallback is stated for that recruitment step, and p.7 E's maximum rule concerns moving pieces onto the board. Neither explicitly authorizes partial Court recruitment or reclaiming board pieces for this special action.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: Only zero or one own Caballero remains in provinces.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: Recruiting the available one, declining/being unable to execute the action, or taking a board substitute yields different court and board states.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Quotes the two-piece effect and expressly discloses the missing shortage procedure.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: When The Court cannot obtain two from provinces, may it recruit the available amount? Is board reclamation allowed for this special action, and from which locations? Specify the zero-piece case.

essential_branches.title: Forced Movement: Castillo destination permission versus secret-disk domain
source_references: PDF p.2, secret disk excludes Castillo
PDF p.7 C and F, general Castillo destination permission
essential_branches.source_problem: General rules permit any/all Caballeros moved by special actions to enter Castillo. The forced Movement action instead directs each affected player to choose a destination on a disk that cannot name Castillo. It does not state an exception to the general permission or an alternative way to declare Castillo.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: A fellow player whose group is being expelled wants to send that group to Castillo.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: Excluding Castillo, allowing an extra declaration, or allowing an indicated board destination plus diversion/splitting produce different legal destinations and piece distributions.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Preserves the disk procedure, court fallback and protected origins, and explicitly discloses the Castillo destination conflict instead of silently deciding it.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Can the forced Movement card send any expelled Caballeros to Castillo? If yes, how is that choice made secretly with the original disk, and must the entire player's group share that destination? If not, explicitly establish this card's exception to p.7 C/F.
essential_branches.resolved_domains: King's region cannot be emptied; Castillo cannot be emptied before general scoring. These are explicit p.7 restrictions, not unresolved origin alternatives.

essential_branches.title: All-4 special scoring when Castillo has mobile 4/0/0
source_references: PDF p.10, all-4 scoring and all-5 exclusion
PDF p.11, mobile scoreboard may be placed at Castillo
PDF pp.2 and 4, nine regions versus special Castillo location
essential_branches.source_problem: A mobile 4/0/0 may legally cover Castillo's scoreboard. All-4 scoring uses current first values and says to score all regions with four lilies, but does not expressly include or exclude Castillo. The source treats Castillo separately from nine regions while expressly including/excluding it in other scoring-card texts; the all-5 card explicitly excludes it.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: Place 4/0/0 at a nonempty Castillo and execute an all-4 scoring action.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: Scoring Castillo awards points and reveals contents; excluding it does neither. Ordinary board-region mobile category changes are expressly resolved and are not gaps.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Correctly handles mobile category replacement for board regions and expressly flags the Castillo/all-4 intersection as unresolved.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Does all-4 scoring include Castillo when its current scoreboard is mobile 4/0/0, or do value-category scorings always exclude Castillo? If it is included, confirm it is revealed, scored using the mobile values, and re-covered without redistribution.

essential_branches.title: Zero-count scoring eligibility is not explicitly defined
essential_branches.candidate_status: Additional completeness candidate; less certain than E01–E07 because ordinary-language 'players with Caballeros' may be understood to exclude absence.
source_references: PDF pp.5–6, rank/tie rules and examples
PDF p.11, least-Caballeros card explicitly excludes empty regions
essential_branches.source_problem: The general scoring text supplies rankings and tie shifts but no express minimum of one Caballero to qualify for a rank. Its examples involve positive counts only. Under a purely numeric ranking, absent players can occupy a payable rank or an entirely empty region can pay tied-second points; the usual occupied-player interpretation would not.
essential_branches.reachable_trigger: In a five-player game, a 5/3/1 region has counts 2,0,0,0,0; or the region is empty.
essential_branches.outcome_branch: Ignoring zero counts versus treating them as tied numeric counts changes point awards during ordinary general scoring.
summary_references: snapshot Region ranks, ties and bonuses, especially line 152
essential_branches.summary_reason: Faithfully reproduces the source's positive-count ranking/tie scheme without supplying an unsupported minimum-presence rule. It does not label this additional possible omission.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Confirm whether a player must have at least one Caballero in a scored region/Castillo to earn any rank points, and whether an entirely empty scored location awards no points. Explain how zero counts are excluded before tie/rank calculation.
essential_branches.caution: Do not treat the familiar no-pieces/no-points convention as verified for this exact source without matching primary authority. Complete-core FAIL already follows from the high-confidence findings, independently of this candidate.

essential_branches.title: The King returns participant mismatch is resolved internally
source_references: PDF p.7, consult detailed explanation when meaning is unclear
PDF p.9, heading versus detailed explanation and printed card
essential_branches.source_problem: The heading says fellow players, but the detailed explanation says each player in clockwise order and the pictured card also says each player.
essential_branches.resolution_from_permitted_source: Use the detailed explanation and agreeing card face: the selecting player participates, last in that clockwise sequence. This does not supply a shortage rule.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Explicitly identifies the wording discrepancy and explains its source-grounded choice.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: None for participation; E01 still requires shortage clarification.

essential_branches.title: Secret return cards: selecting disks and removing pieces are distinct duties
source_references: PDF p.9, secretly remove two card face, heading and detail
PDF p.10, secretly remove all card face, heading and detail
essential_branches.source_problem: Card faces and headings assign removal to fellow players; the explanation instructs all players to select disks. It does not expressly say the selecting player must remove pieces. These sentences can coexist as all-player disk participation with fellow-player removal, so 'all players select' alone does not establish that the selector loses Caballeros.
essential_branches.classification_reason: When every participant has a legal disk choice, whether an otherwise unaffected selector also sets a disk does not by itself alter the resulting piece state. The exact disk choreography remains a procedural limitation. When mandatory all-player selection has no legal occupied region, the executable-action branch is essential and is covered by E03/E04.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Separately preserves fellow-player removal and the all-player disk wording, and does not invent a requirement for the selector to return pieces.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Confirm whether the selecting player sets a disk purely as an unaffected participant, whether its choice must satisfy the same occupancy condition, and how an unaffected player without a qualifying region participates. Do not infer selector removal merely from disk participation.

essential_branches.title: Intrigue's 'only these cards' statement conflicts with explicit forced Movement
source_references: PDF p.8, introductory claim that only intrigue cards move another player's Caballeros
essential_branches.source_problem: The broad introductory claim is overinclusive if read to prohibit the explicit forced Movement card.
essential_branches.resolution_from_permitted_source: The detailed Movement action expressly requires fellow players to move their own groups. The selecting player is not given arbitrary control over individual foreign pieces. The specific action is playable subject to E06's destination issue.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Provides the actual card effects rather than importing the misleading broad prohibition.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: None to execute the explicit Movement effect; E06 remains separate.

essential_branches.title: No additional final-score tiebreaker
essential_branches.source_problem: The source identifies the furthest success-track position but gives no further tiebreaker for equal maximum positions.
essential_branches.classification_reason: The game can finish and the maximum-scoring players can be identified without another gameplay transition. A requirement to produce exactly one winner would need an added rule, but this omission alone need not prevent completing the base game.
essential_branches.summary_reason: Expressly says no additional endgame tiebreaker is provided.
essential_branches.exact_clarification_needed: Only if a single-winner adjudication is required: confirm the original edition's tied-outcome policy. Do not invent a tiebreak.

resolution_result: Bounded research supplied no independently publisher-verified resolution for all exact essential gaps. No later edition or self-claimed approval was silently substituted.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: The King returns requires each player to return three eligible own Caballeros from regions and/or court, excluding the King’s region and Castillo. No shortfall procedure is specified when fewer than three eligible pieces exist.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: An affected player can lack three removable pieces; the summary cannot determine how to finish this action from the source alone.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: Send one from each player has no fallback when a player has no Caballero in any eligible region. Courts, Castillo and the King’s region are not eligible origins.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: The selecting player may be unable to select the required one piece for a color.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: Secret removal of two requires a region containing at least two own Caballeros. Its singleton fallback is conditioned on having at most one in every region, while the King’s region is protected. It provides no explicit no-piece procedure, or fallback for a player with a protected pair and only eligible singletons.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: There can be no permitted disk choice satisfying the printed selection condition. No source-backed substitute execution is available.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: Secret removal of all from one region exempts a player with no pieces in any region, but does not explain selection when the player’s only regional pieces occupy the protected King’s region.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: The player has pieces in a region but cannot legally remove them or select an eligible occupied region.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: Both secret-removal card headings and card faces address fellow players, whereas the detailed paragraphs say all players simultaneously select regions. The source does not reconcile the selecting player’s disk participation.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: Who must perform the secret selection is ambiguous. The summary reports both formulations and does not silently change the card’s stated removal targets.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: The general action rule permits any or all moved Caballeros to go to Castillo. The forced Movement card uses secret disks, which omit Castillo, without explicitly reconciling that general permission.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: Whether and how an affected player may send the forced group into Castillo cannot be settled definitively from these pages. The summary describes the printed disk procedure and separately flags the unresolved conflict.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: All-4 special scoring refers to all regions whose first value is four and mobile scoreboards override printed values. A 4/0/0 scoreboard may be placed at Castillo; the source does not expressly state Castillo’s inclusion or exclusion for this combination. The all-5 card explicitly excludes Castillo.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: A reachable scoreboard placement creates an unresolved special-scoring inclusion question; the summary flags it instead of asserting an exception.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: The Court says to move two own Caballeros from provinces to court, without an explicit shortfall rule. The ordinary power-card recruitment shortage rule is described separately and is not expressly extended to this special action.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: If provinces contain fewer than two, the source does not explicitly supply the missing execution procedure. The summary preserves this limitation.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: Multi-origin four-piece intrigue effects say other regions, while some three-piece effects say any regions. No example defines whether other excludes each piece’s own origin or every selected origin collectively.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: A strict universal ban on all selected origins as destinations would be an unsupported additional rule. The summary preserves the destination wording and explicitly declines that extra inference.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: The King returns heading says fellow players, but both the detailed execution paragraph and card face say each player. Page 7 directs readers to detailed explanations when meaning is unclear.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Transparently follows each player, including the selecting player, and states the conflicting heading.
final_source_audit_limitations.impact: This is a supported, disclosed use of the detailed explanation and matching card face, rather than an unsupported conflict resolution.

final_source_audit_limitations.description: The source names the player furthest on the success track as winner and gives no additional endgame tiebreaker.
final_source_audit_limitations.summary_treatment: Accurately states that no additional tiebreaker is supplied.

additional_final_clarification.multi_origin_other_regions: For each affected classic Intrigue effect, does other regions exclude only the individual piece’s origin or every selected origin collectively? Specify whether moves between two selected origin regions are legal; give an applicable classic-English example.
additional_final_clarification.actor_disk_participation: Clarify exact affected/participating players and legal disk choice when selector lacks an eligible region. Earlier reviewers distinguish harmless extra choreography from state-changing no-legal-choice branches; final audit conservatively flags participation as essential.
